course: Middle-school life science, grade 6: traits, inheritance and choosing what to grow
curriculum: Living things pass traits to their offspring

Two parents each give half, so the young are not copies

Counting the offspring, and comparing counts with what was expected
Punnett squares: writing down what a cross can produce
Same seed, different field: what a plant looks like depends on where it grew
A fair test needs a control and everything else kept the same
Repeats and averages: one plant proves nothing
Choosing which plants to breed from, and what that costs
Choosing for one trait can drag another along with it
Variety inside a collection, and why losing it is hard to undo
How many plants you need to keep a kind going
A label and a record are part of the seed
Disease arrives, and resistance is a trait like any other
Deciding with a season that does not come round again
